extracted.intended_audience: Investigators (PD/PI, co-investigators, key personnel) preparing NIH biographical sketches for grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing an NIH-style Biographical Sketch (Biosketch) to include identification, education/training, Personal Statement, Positions and Honors, Contributions to Science, and Research Support for a grant application. Follows NIH biographical sketch template and page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the entire biosketch to five pages maximum; be concise and prioritize the most relevant information for the grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification fields
rubrics_metrics.description: NAME; eRA COMMONS USER NAME (credential, e.g., agency login); POSITION TITLE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full name, eRA Commons user name, and current position title at the top of the biosketch so the applicant is unambiguously identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education/Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with baccalaureate or other initial professional education, such as nursing, include postdoctoral training and residency training if applicable. Add/delete rows as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide institution and location, degree (if applicable), completion date (MM/YYYY), and field of study in a tabular format. Start with the earliest (baccalaureate) entry and include all relevant training up to postdoctoral/residency as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section A — Personal Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal Statement (A) — summary of the investigator's background, major accomplishments, relevance to the proposed project, and prior mentoring/leadership experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the investigator is well suited for the role on the project: describe prior related work, leadership of relevant programs/labs, mentorship record (e.g., number of PhD/postdocs trained), prior role on related grants (e.g., served as primary mentor for a K award), and specific contributions the investigator will make to the proposed research (e.g., lead analytic lab, contribute to PK analyses). Use concrete examples and link to prior work that directly informs the current aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section B — Positions and Honors
rubrics_metrics.description: Positions and Employment and Honors — chronological list of appointments (with dates) and honors/awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List academic and professional positions with year ranges (e.g., 1965-69 Assistant Professor...), leadership roles, editorial positions, committee service, and honors (fellowships, awards, honorary degrees). Dates and titles should be clear so reviewers can assess experience and stature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section C — Contributions to Science
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributions to Science — narrative descriptions of major scientific contributions, each with illustrative representative publications (citations numbered from the publication list).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each major contribution, provide a concise narrative describing the scientific advance and its significance, followed by representative cited publications (with citation numbers referencing the applicant's publication list). Where helpful, include citation impact/context (e.g., citation counts, journal recognitions) to document influence. Use numbered subheadings (e.g., 1. Clinical Pharmacokinetics) and include specific landmark papers and their influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section D — Research Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Support — list ongoing and completed research support with grant number, agency, PI, dates, project title, brief description of aims, investigator's role (e.g., Role: PI, Role: Co-Investigator) and calendar effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate ongoing vs completed support; for each award include grant number (e.g., R01 AI098472), funding agency, PI name, project title, project period (dates), a short description of the project's goals, the investigator's specific role/responsibilities on the project, and the calendar effort expressed (e.g., 0.6 Calendar, 0.9 Calendar). Indicate if institutional funds or other non-NIH sources support lab operations as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide complete publication list link
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete List of Published Work: [URL to MyNCBI publications].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a URL (e.g., http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/myncbi/...) to the applicant's complete publication bibliography so reviewers can access the full list and verify representative citations referenced in Section C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role statements in research support entries
rubrics_metrics.description: For each research support entry, explicitly state the investigator's role (e.g., Role: PI, Role: Co-Investigator) within the grant description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the investigator's contribution to each grant explicit (lead vs collaborator vs analytic support) so reviewers can judge time commitment, overlap with the proposed project, and potential conflicts of commitment.
